To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stable and derived categories of representations of finite groups are stacks on the orbit category of the group, and that the kernel of the homomorphisms between endotrivial groups is determined by the cohomology of a certain simplicial complex, which can be explicitly computed in terms of sipp Cech groups.

the stable category of representations of a finite group G is a stack over the orbit category of the finite group G, that sipp Cech homology can be used to compute endotrivial representations, and that the sipp topology can be used to understand the derived category of representations of finite groups.

the category of representations of a finite group G is a stack of categories, that the category of derived representations is a stack of derived categories, and that the category of stable representations is a stack.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
  1. What is the relationship between the representation theory of a finite group and that of one of its subgroups?
  2. When can a representation of the subgroup be extended to the group?
the following question: how can we use the theory of stacks to understand the restriction of representations from a finite group G to its subgroups H?

the following questions:
  1. What are the derived and stable categories of representations?
  2. How can one construct the derived and stable representations from the plain ones?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sipp topology is the correct Grothendieick topology on the category of G-sets, for the purpose of understanding restriction and induction of representations of finite groups.

the sipp cohomology of a G-module is the cohomology of the corresponding sheaf with respect to the sipp topology, and this is a generalization of the classical socalled Mackey cohomology of G-modules.
sipp Cech theory is a useful tool in the study of group representations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stable category of H-representations is the derived quotient of the stable category of G-representations, with respect to the kernel of the homomorphisms T (G) → T (H), and that the kernel of this homomorphism is precisely the image of the restriction functor.
we have found a way to understand the restriction of a representation of a finite group G to a subgroup H, in terms of the descent theory of stacks.
the category of endotrivial G-sets is a sipp stack, and the category of endo-trivial H-sets is its pull-back along the inclusion of a Sylow H-subgroup into G.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the derived and stable categories of representations are not really categories, but rather stacks of categories.
the theory of stacks can be fruitfully applied to the theory of representations of groups, in particular to the theory of endotrivial modules.
the theory of stacks can be used to study the interplay between group cohomology, representation theory, and the geometry of G-sets.
